summary: Collection sockets on one daemon reread their paced windows on shared steps, so a changed window is computed once instead of once per socket

replay.detail: Collection refresh timing changes only; claim admission and replay are unchanged.

schema.detail: The reread grid's start is kept in memory per store. No database schema or persistent state changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged; no coordinated member upgrade is required.

compatibility.detail: The collection protocol, authorization checks, snapshot fences, current-row diffs, reconnect behavior and which windows reread are unchanged. A window that already delivered its snapshot now rereads on the next shared step at least half an interval after its last read: steadily every 1.5 s as before, but a change can reach it up to 2.25 s after the last reread instead of 1.5 s, and two rereads can be as close as 0.75 s once, when a socket first joins the steps. A first snapshot, including one waiting for a view to publish, is still read at once.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work or interruption beyond a normal daemon restart.

manual.detail: No operator action or client configuration change is needed.

recovery.detail: No persistent changes or new binary swap-back restrictions.
